title: LightPC settings meta-schema
description: Documents the renderer keywords a setting schema may use. Editors map setting.schema.json to this file, so x-drived and x-options are completed and documented instead of being reported as unknown properties. The standard keywords stay unrestricted on purpose, otherwise every type, properties or required would be flagged.

x-drived.description: Marks a derived node: it backs other fields and is never rendered.

x-options.description: Where a select takes its options from. The referenced array is a sibling of the annotated node.

from.description: Sibling array property holding the options.

field.description: Property of each array entry used as the option label; omit it when the entries are already strings.

x-options-when.description: Overrides the option source while a boolean setting is enabled.

key.description: Sibling property that switches the source, evaluated on the same object as the annotated node.

x-units.description: Units a value may carry, in one of three shapes: a field naming a set declared on the document root, a field listing its own units, or the root holding the sets as a name to list map. The list is a rendering reference, not a setting, so it never shows up as a field.

oneOf.description: Name of a set declared on the document root, for example "time".
Sets declared once on the root, so a field only has to name one.
Units declared inline for this field alone. Use it when a value needs a set no shared group covers, so the root map does not grow a one-off entry.

x-number.description: Regular expression the number half of a value must match before it is committed, for example "^\\d+(\\.\\d+)?". It constrains the value at the control, while pattern constrains the whole document string.
